This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Shared conventions

The portfolio’s shared rules are synced into .claude/shared/ from pedrobtz/packages:claude/shared/. Never edit them here. Where this file and a shared file disagree, this file wins for this package.

@.claude/shared/workflow.md @.claude/shared/r-package.md @.claude/shared/ci.md @.claude/shared/correctness.md @.claude/shared/assurance.md

What this is

zubin is an R package for structured binary data, and two products in one:

  1. An R API over raw vectors, prefixed bin_: record layouts (bin_layout()), vectorised bin_unpack()/bin_pack(), homogeneous codecs bin_decode()/bin_encode(), a byte builder (bin_builder(), bin_put(), bin_take()), bin_hexdump()/bin_diff(), and from Stage 10 bin_serialize(), bin_unserialize() and bin_hash_object() over zubin-r.h’s zb_serialize(), zb_unserialize() and zb_serialize_to_sink().
  2. A header-only C99 library under inst/include/zubin/, consumed through LinkingTo: zubin, zufast alone: a buffer with ownership and limits, a checked cursor, typed reads and writes at any alignment and byte order, and layout kernels.

The headers are built on zufast’s (<zufast/bits.h>, <zufast/utf8.h>); zubin never re-implements a primitive zufast has. Nothing is vendored. It is a member of the zu* family (sibling checkouts in ../: zufast is the closest model, then zukomp, zucrypt, zucbor).

The specification outranks this file:

  • .agents/design.md is the spec, numbered §1–§20; every statement in it is a decision, and open questions live only in its §19 decision log. A stage that changes a decision edits design.md in the same commit.
  • .agents/roadmap.md sequences it into stages, each with a Status: line under its heading. Never put status in a heading: it changes the anchor that the stage issues link to.
  • .agents/next.md holds everything after 0.1.0.
  • .agents/benchmarks.md holds the benchmark results; ideas.md and domains.md feed next.md.

Current state

0.1.0 is on CRAN (published 2026-11-11; tag and release 0.1.0), and main is at 0.1.0.9000, working towards v0.1.1. Stages 0–9 and 10–12 are done (Stage 10: serialisation streams, #25; Stage 11: #26’s small items; Stage 12: what zunpy, zumsgpack, zuint and zuarrow call, #38). Stage 13, the foreign-buffer contract (#40), is planned for v0.1.1 and lands before any sibling’s zero-copy stage. A release is recorded by committing the CRAN-SUBMISSION that devtools::submit_cran() writes: cran-release.yaml tags that commit and opens the .9000 bump. #32 and .agents/next.md hold what follows.

  • Headers: zubin.h and zubin/{version,status,rw,buf,cursor,layout,column}.h (layout.h: types, spec parser, unpack and pack kernels; column.h: bitmaps, validity, swaps), zubin/detail/portability.h, plus zubin-r.h. Stage 12 added u128, i128, c64, c128 (type values 32–35), native-order kernels and the foreign buffer.
  • R API: bin_info(), bin_layout(), bin_size(), bin_unpack(), bin_pack(), bin_decode(), bin_encode(), the builder (bin_builder(), bin_put() raw/typed/"z"/"s<n>", bin_reserve(), bin_reset(), bin_take(), as.raw()), bin_hexdump()/bin_diff(), and the serialisation streams.
  • zufast comes from CRAN; the workflows without R (the header gate, the fuzzers) check out its 0.1.0 tag, never its main.
  • tools/zubintest is the consumer fixture (consumer.yaml); the c-api article renders its recipe from the fixture’s files, so the fixture is the one place to edit.

Versions and dependents

The current version’s parent issue is #2, v0.1.0 (milestone v0.1.0), with stage issues #4 (Stage 0) to #13 (Stage 9), then #25, #26, #38 and #40 for Stages 10–13. One pull request per stage, branch stage-N-<slug>; close the stage issue and update its Status: line in that pull request.

Sibling packages that link to zubin before CRAN does, through LinkingTo and Remotes:: zunpy (pedrobtz/zubin@main), zumsgpack and rdz. zuint and zuarrow are planned consumers of the foreign buffer (Stage 13). A change to a header in inst/include/ breaks them even before 0.1.0.

Commands

tools/check-headers                                # header gate (CC/CXX, ZUFAST_INCLUDE)
tools/run-symbol-audit                             # R CMD check's compiled-code scan, on the probe
CC=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/clang tools/run-fuzz # libFuzzer; Apple clang has none
tools/run-benchmarks                               # the numbers in .agents/benchmarks.md
_R_CHECK_SYSTEM_CLOCK_=0 Rscript -e 'devtools::check(cran = TRUE)'
Rscript -e 'devtools::build_readme()'              # README.Rmd -> README.md
Rscript -e 'pkgdown::build_site()'                 # site -> docs/ (gitignored)
air format R/                                      # format R sources (air defaults)

zufast is on CRAN (install.packages("zufast")); test unreleased zufast changes from the sibling checkout (R CMD INSTALL ../zufast). roxygen2 must be 8.1.0 or newer (Config/roxygen2/version); an older one rewrites man/.

The R fuzz targets (fuzz_serialize, fuzz_sink) embed R through tools/fuzz/rfuzz.c; run them with R_HOME set (tools/run-fuzz does). tools/alloc-exercise.R is what the allocation-failure sweep runs.

Architecture

  • inst/include/zubin/ is the product most consumers see; src/ is thin. src/zubin_r.c holds the .Call entry points over the headers, src/zubin_r.h defines the ZB_INT_R_ON_NEW/FREE hooks the harness counts live buffers through, and src/zubin_test.c holds the test-only zubin_test_ symbols the C-level tests call.
  • R/ is one file per area: layout.R, unpack.R, pack.R, builder.R, hexdump.R, serialize.R, info.R, with checks.R (argument checks) and conditions.R (status names to classes).
  • tools/abi/ holds the ABI probes (probe-none.c, probe-all.c, probe-r.c) that abi.yaml compiles; tools/fuzz/ the libFuzzer targets and seeds; tools/zubintest/ the consumer fixture package.

In C, zb_field.count is the byte width for b, s and x fields; the element count of a column is 1 for them. Alignment is zb_type_align(), not the width: a complex type aligns as its part. A 128-bit value is a zb_u128 (lo first), a container with no arithmetic.

zubin-r.h’s serialisation streams are the one place R raises: R’s errors during R_Serialize/R_Unserialize (a malformed stream, a refhook) reach the caller unchanged; only EOF (zb_unserialize, via R_tryCatch on a private condition class) and a builder that cannot grow (zb_serialize, with R_UnwindProtect restoring its length on a jump) are statuses.

The .Call convention: an entry point that can fail returns, on failure, a zubin_status-classed string holding the zb_status enumerator name (attribute index when an element is at fault); R checks is_status() and raises through zb_fail(), which maps the name to a class with zb_status_class. C never calls Rf_error() except in the test harness.

Invariants that are easy to break

Linkage (design §4.5):

  1. Every function defined in a header is static inline (ZB_INLINE), never plain static.
  2. Consumers, and zubin itself, compile with PKG_CFLAGS = $(C_VISIBILITY); zubin.so exports R_init_zubin and nothing else (test-abi.R).
  3. The headers reference nothing R CMD check forbids in compiled code: no printf, abort, exit, assert, rand, stdout, stderr (tools/run-symbol-audit).
  4. No R header and no SEXP under inst/include/zubin/; only zubin-r.h includes R.
  5. Never compare function pointers taken from a header-only function: each translation unit has its own copy. Ownership and growability are flags in zb_buf.

Allocation and errors:

  • No allocation anywhere in the headers except buf.h, and there only via malloc, realloc, free. No bare size arithmetic: zb_size_add()/zb_size_mul().
  • No static object under inst/include/zubin/: every header promises any thread may call it (design §15), and tools/check-headers enforces it. zubin-r.h is main-thread only.
  • On any failure the inputs are unchanged: a cursor that fails has not advanced, a buffer that fails holds what it held. Tests check this at every truncation point.
  • Heap state that must survive a longjmp is owned by R before the first call that can jump (design §12): zb_r_buf_new() registers the finalizer before the buffer exists. The harness counts live buffers through the ZB_INT_R_ON_NEW/FREE hooks defined in src/zubin_r.h; test-lifetime.R asserts the count returns to baseline after gc().
  • C never raises below the outermost .Call; statuses map to condition classes by enumerator name in R/conditions.R, and the call is reduced to the function name.
  • Offsets are 0-based everywhere (§14.1). Byte order is never guessed (§14.2).

Testing

  • Byte-explicit: inputs are hex strings through bytes().
  • Serial: no Config/testthat/parallel, so gctorture and valgrind instrument this package’s C.
  • No file-scope objects, because shuffling reorders top-level code as well as tests: anything two tests share goes in a helper-*.R file (helper-abi.R, helper-bytes.R, helper-expect.R, helper-layout.R, helper-rw.R, helper-serialize.R, helper-skip.R), never at file scope in a test-*.R.
  • Compare doubles bit for bit with bits() when NaN payloads or -0 matter.
  • Never write an expected double as a long decimal literal: R’s parser on macOS arm64 rounds some to a neighbouring double. Use exact forms (2^-24, -2^1000) or bytes.
  • tests/testthat/fixtures/golden.tsv is data: generated once outside the repository from an independent encoder, read with colClasses = "character", never regenerated by a test. The arch legs depend on it: the golden vectors must decode to the same values on i386, musl and big-endian s390x (design §15).
  • Exhaustive sweeps and big buffers sit behind ZUBIN_SLOW_TESTS=true, which the full R CMD check profile sets; tests that allocate heavily call skip_heavy() (ZUBIN_SKIP_HEAVY, set by the gctorture leg).
  • Design §13.1, the roxygen table and the tests are the same table three times.

Continuous integration

A deviation from ci.md: every r-actions workflow except R-CMD-check.yaml is pinned by commit to a release, with the tag in a trailing comment, not only those that hold a write token; Dependabot bumps them. R-CMD-check.yaml and native-checks.yaml do not pass profile: auto: they run quick on a pull request and full on every push to main, and the full-ci label runs the full set on a pull request. Each workflow landed at the stage that gave it something to check (roadmap, “CI, and the stage each workflow lands in”).

Workflow What it checks
R-CMD-check.yaml r-actions’ runners plus Windows R-devel (CRAN’s flavour, which the Linux containers miss), nosuggests; the full profile sets ZUBIN_SLOW_TESTS
native-checks.yaml UBSan, ASan, valgrind, LTO, gctorture, analyzers and a blocking rchk (through r-actions with github-packages)
coverage.yaml coverage, and the badge under .github/badges/
pkgdown.yaml the site, development: mode: auto
abi.yaml (own) headers compile standalone as C99 and C++11, the include-everything and call-everything probes are warning-free under GCC and clang, then the symbol audit (design §16.1)
consumer.yaml (own) tools/zubintest checks with no compiled-code NOTE, defines no global zb_ or zuf_ symbol, and still loads with zubin and zufast uninstalled (design §16.5)
hardening.yaml canaries first, then fuzz_layout, fuzz_unpack, fuzz_buf, fuzz_serialize, fuzz_sink through r-actions’ fuzz.yml, corpus cached: ten minutes a target per push, an hour nightly (design §16.6)
arch.yaml the suite on i386, musl and s390x under QEMU, weekly
alloc-failure.yaml r-actions’ allocation-failure sweep over tools/alloc-exercise.R; informational, weekly and by hand, never on a pull request
benchmarks.yaml (own) tools/run-benchmarks on Linux; by hand, and on pull requests that change the benchmarks

The fuzzers and the header gate fetch zufast’s headers at its CRAN tag (github-packages in r-actions), not its main. Issue #94 tracks gating the jobs that still run on documentation-only pull requests.

Editing rules specific to zubin

  • Prose is en-GB (Language: en-GB); domain terms go in inst/WORDLIST.
  • README.md is generated: edit README.Rmd and run devtools::build_readme().
  • The c-api article renders from tools/zubintest; edit the fixture, not the article’s code.
